# SolarSystemResource

> Domain research archive for the Solar System. Literature reviews and primary-source analyses. Curated by Corgan Studio, Inc.

Research Archive: https://solarsystemresource.com/research/ (literature reviews by Corgan Studio, Inc., open to read).

## Research Archive

- [Interstellar objects: 'Oumuamua, 2I/Borisov and 3I/ATLAS](https://solarsystemresource.com/research/interstellar-objects): Review of the three confirmed interstellar objects to pass through the Solar System: their discovery circumstances, hyperbolic orbits, physical and compositional properties, the debate over 'Oumuamua's non-gravitational acceleration, and the detection and intercept prospects of the Rubin era.
- [Kuiper Belt population statistics: classical, resonant, and scattered components](https://solarsystemresource.com/research/kuiper-belt-population-statistics): Review of the Kuiper Belt population structure as resolved by the Outer Solar System Origins Survey (OSSOS) and successor programs, with focus on the cold-vs-hot classical dichotomy, resonant trapping, and the scattered disc that supplies the Centaurs.
- [Near-Earth object catalog gaps and survey completeness](https://solarsystemresource.com/research/neo-survey-completeness): Review of the Near-Earth Object catalog completeness as of 2026, the contributions of the Catalina Sky Survey, ATLAS, Pan-STARRS, and the upcoming NEO Surveyor mission, and the residual gap in detection of dark and small NEOs.
- [Mean motion resonances and the Nice model of giant-planet migration](https://solarsystemresource.com/research/nice-model-resonances): Review of the Nice model of giant-planet migration during the Late Heavy Bombardment, the role of mean-motion resonance crossings (particularly Jupiter-Saturn 2:1) in driving the migration, and the observational predictions tested by Trojan and Kuiper Belt populations.
- [Planetary migration and the Nice model: dynamical evidence](https://solarsystemresource.com/research/planetary-migration-nice-model): Review of the Nice model of giant-planet migration, the dynamical evidence from Trojan asymmetry and Kuiper Belt structure, and the Late Heavy Bombardment timing constraints that the model addresses.
- [Dwarf planet inventory beyond Neptune](https://solarsystemresource.com/research/trans-neptunian-dwarfs): Review of the trans-Neptunian dwarf-planet population - Pluto, Eris, Makemake, Haumea, plus the unconfirmed candidates Quaoar, Sedna, Gonggong, Salacia, Orcus, Varuna, and the expected Vera C. Rubin Observatory contribution to the inventory.
